results.name: unsupported_far_target_floor
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets that lie outside the [min,max] example range, more than 5 away from every example, and belong to no small rule (<=20 members, of the model's 45) containing all examples; observed above null means people have a guessing/lapse floor the model lacks, below null means they reject such targets even more firmly.
results.code:
# name: unsupported_far_target_floor
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets that lie outside the [min,max] example range, more than 5 away from every example, and belong to no small rule (<=20 members, of the model's 45) containing all examples; observed above null means people have a guessing/lapse floor the model lacks, below null means they reject such targets even more firmly.
def test_statistic(df):
    N = np.arange(1, 101)
    rules = [N % 2 == 1, N % 2 == 0,
             np.array([n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1)) for n in N]),
             np.isin(N, [n * n for n in range(1, 11)]), np.isin(N, [n ** 3 for n in range(1, 5)]),
             np.isin(N, [2, 4, 8, 16, 64]), np.isin(N, [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64])]
    for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]:
        rules.append(N % m == 0)
    for m in range(2, 11):
        rules.append(np.isin(N, [m ** k for k in range(1, 8) if m ** k <= 100]))
    for d in range(10):
        rules.append(N % 10 == d)
        rules.append(np.array([str(d) in str(n) for n in N]))
    M = np.array(rules)
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    s_arr = sets.to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    sel = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for s in sets.unique():
        e = np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")])
        ok = M[:, e - 1].all(axis=1) & (M.sum(axis=1) <= 20)
        cover = M[ok].any(axis=0) if ok.any() else np.zeros(100, dtype=bool)
        far = np.abs(N[:, None] - e[None, :]).min(axis=1) > 5
        good = far & ~cover & ((N < e.min()) | (N > e.max()))
        idx = s_arr == s
        sel[idx] = good[t[idx] - 1]
    return float(r[sel].mean()) if sel.any() else 0.0

results.name: set_level_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across example sets (sets with >=18 trials) of each set's overall yes rate; observed above null means people's overall willingness to generalize differs between sets more than the model predicts, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: set_level_yes_rate_sd
# description: Standard deviation across example sets (sets with >=18 trials) of each set's overall yes rate; observed above null means people's overall willingness to generalize differs between sets more than the model predicts, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.assign(rr=df["rating"].astype(float)).groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str))["rr"].agg(["mean", "count"])
    g = g[g["count"] >= 18]
    return float(g["mean"].std()) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: upward_minus_downward_extension
results.description: Among non-example targets outside the example range and within 15 of it, yes rate for targets above the max example minus targets below the min example; observed above null means people extend generalization upward more than the model's symmetric interval hypotheses predict, below null means downward more.
results.code:
# name: upward_minus_downward_extension
# description: Among non-example targets outside the example range and within 15 of it, yes rate for targets above the max example minus targets below the min example; observed above null means people extend generalization upward more than the model's symmetric interval hypotheses predict, below null means downward more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    lo = ex.min(axis=1); hi = ex.max(axis=1)
    up = (t > hi) & (t - hi <= 15)
    dn = (t < lo) & (lo - t <= 15)
    if up.sum() == 0 or dn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[up].mean() - r[dn].mean())

results.name: shared_last_digit_set_nonmember_yes
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets whose last digit differs from the common last digit, among sets of >=2 examples that all share one last digit; observed below null means people reject non-members of an "ends in d" concept more sharply than the model's single tempered size principle allows (above null means less sharply).
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_set_nonmember_yes
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets whose last digit differs from the common last digit, among sets of >=2 examples that all share one last digit; observed below null means people reject non-members of an "ends in d" concept more sharply than the model's single tempered size principle allows (above null means less sharply).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = ex.notna().sum(axis=1)
    ld = ex % 10
    shared = (ld.nunique(axis=1) == 1) & (n >= 2)
    d = ld.iloc[:, 0]
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    mask = shared & (~inset) & ((t % 10) != d)
    return float(r[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: parity_within_min_rule
results.description: For sets whose examples all share parity, among non-example targets in the smallest consistent non-parity rule (multiples of k, squares, powers, ends-in/contains-digit, etc.) that contains both parities, yes rate for same-parity targets minus opposite-parity targets; observed above null means people form parity conjunctions (e.g. odd multiples of 3) more than the model's union of single rules predicts.
results.code:
# name: parity_within_min_rule
# description: For sets whose examples all share parity, among non-example targets in the smallest consistent non-parity rule (multiples of k, squares, powers, ends-in/contains-digit, etc.) that contains both parities, yes rate for same-parity targets minus opposite-parity targets; observed above null means people form parity conjunctions (e.g. odd multiples of 3) more than the model's union of single rules predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    N = np.arange(1, 101)
    rules = [np.isin(N, [n * n for n in range(1, 11)]), np.isin(N, [n ** 3 for n in range(1, 5)])]
    for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]:
        rules.append(N % m == 0)
    for m in range(2, 11):
        rules.append(np.isin(N, [m ** k for k in range(1, 8) if m ** k <= 100]))
    for d in range(10):
        rules.append(np.array([str(d) in str(n) for n in N]))
    M = np.array(rules)
    mixed = (M & (N % 2 == 0)).any(axis=1) & (M & (N % 2 == 1)).any(axis=1)
    sizes = M.sum(axis=1)
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    s_arr = sets.to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mem = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    same = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    valid = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for s in sets.unique():
        e = np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")])
        if len(set(e % 2)) != 1:
            continue
        ok = M[:, e - 1].all(axis=1) & mixed
        if not ok.any():
            continue
        i = np.where(ok)[0][np.argmin(sizes[ok])]
        idx = s_arr == s
        valid[idx] = True
        mem[idx] = M[i][t[idx] - 1] & ~np.isin(t[idx], e)
        same[idx] = (t[idx] % 2) == (e[0] % 2)
    a = valid & mem & same; b = valid & mem & ~same
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: math_rule_member_contrast
results.description: For sets whose smallest consistent rule is an arithmetic rule (squares, cubes, primes, multiples of k, powers of k; size <= 35), yes rate of non-example targets in that rule minus non-example targets outside it; observed below null means people discriminate members of arithmetic concepts less than the model predicts (above null means more).
results.code:
# name: math_rule_member_contrast
# description: For sets whose smallest consistent rule is an arithmetic rule (squares, cubes, primes, multiples of k, powers of k; size <= 35), yes rate of non-example targets in that rule minus non-example targets outside it; observed below null means people discriminate members of arithmetic concepts less than the model predicts (above null means more).
def test_statistic(df):
    N = np.arange(1, 101)
    rules = []
    rules.append(np.isin(N, [n * n for n in range(1, 11)]))
    rules.append(np.isin(N, [n ** 3 for n in range(1, 5)]))
    rules.append(np.array([n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1)) for n in N]))
    for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]:
        rules.append(N % m == 0)
    for m in range(2, 11):
        rules.append(np.isin(N, [m ** k for k in range(1, 8) if m ** k <= 100]))
    M = np.array(rules)  # (R,100)
    sizes = M.sum(axis=1)
    # digit rules also compete for "smallest"
    D = np.array([(N % 10) == d for d in range(10)] + [np.array([str(d) in str(n) for n in N]) for d in range(10)])
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    uniq = sets.unique()
    mem_tab = {}
    for s in uniq:
        e = np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) - 1
        ok = M[:, e].all(axis=1)
        okd = D[:, e].all(axis=1)
        best_d = D.sum(axis=1)[okd].min() if okd.any() else 999
        if ok.any():
            i = np.where(ok)[0][np.argmin(sizes[ok])]
            if sizes[i] <= 35 and sizes[i] < best_d:
                mem_tab[s] = M[i]
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    s_arr = sets.to_numpy()
    valid = np.array([x in mem_tab for x in s_arr])
    if not valid.any():
        return 0.0
    mem = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for s, row in mem_tab.items():
        idx = s_arr == s
        mem[idx] = row[t[idx] - 1]
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    inset = ex.eq(df["target"].astype(int), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    a = valid & ~inset & mem; b = valid & ~inset & ~mem
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: round_number_residual
results.description: Among non-example targets, mean over multiple-of-10 targets of (rating minus that set's mean rating over non-example targets); observed below null means people under-endorse round numbers relative to the model (above null means over-endorse).
results.code:
# name: round_number_residual
# description: Among non-example targets, mean over multiple-of-10 targets of (rating minus that set's mean rating over non-example targets); observed below null means people under-endorse round numbers relative to the model (above null means over-endorse).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    d = pd.DataFrame({"s": df["number_set"].astype(str), "r": r, "t": t})[~inset]
    resid = d["r"] - d.groupby("s")["r"].transform("mean")
    m = (d["t"] % 10) == 0
    return float(resid[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: tens_digit_match_outside_range
results.description: Among non-example targets outside the [min,max] example range, yes rate for targets sharing a tens digit (decade) with some example minus those that do not; observed above null means people generalize by decade similarity beyond what the model's intervals/rules predict, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: tens_digit_match_outside_range
# description: Among non-example targets outside the [min,max] example range, yes rate for targets sharing a tens digit (decade) with some example minus those that do not; observed above null means people generalize by decade similarity beyond what the model's intervals/rules predict, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    inset = ex.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    outside = (t < ex.min(axis=1)) | (t > ex.max(axis=1))
    dec = (ex // 10).where(ex < 100, 9)
    tdec = (t // 10).where(t < 100, 9)
    share = dec.eq(tdec, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    base = outside & (~inset)
    a = base & share; b = base & (~share)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
